newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Street fighting breaks out in Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: Street fighting breaks out in Belgrade.

text.p: Street fighting between government and opposition demonstrators erupted in Belgrade on Tuesday after Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic brought thousands of supporters to the capital in a show of strength.

Eyewitnesses said rival groups fought each other with sticks and iron bars as scuffles broke out among the crowds converging on the city centre headquarters of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition.
There was no immediate police intervention as 35 days of peaceful Zajedno protests against election fraud by Milosevic's ruling socialists turned ugly.
The Socialist Party (SPS) called its demonstration at the same place where Zajedno has held daily demonstrations in what opposition sources said was a clear act of provocation.
There were fears that the SPS might use the violence as an excuse to ban future demonstrations or even to declare a state of emergency.
Milosevic, under threat of Western reprisals, has not so far used his police against the demonstrations, the biggest since 1992 when he used tanks to quell unrest.
